summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of coronary artery disease, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and prior stent placement was admitted for recurrent chest pain that awoke him from sleep, accompanied by progressive shortness of breath. The chest pain improved with nitroglycerin but was concerning for cardiac ischemia. Evaluation revealed no acute myocardial infarction, but a dobutamine stress echo showed ischemic changes. Chest imaging demonstrated pulmonary edema likely due to heart failure, supported by markedly elevated BNP. The patient had missed a dialysis session and presented with hypertensive urgency. He underwent inpatient hemodialysis, which improved his symptoms. Medications were optimized, including switching from metoprolol to carvedilol and increasing doses of amlodipine and isosorbide mononitrate. The patient stabilized, remained asymptomatic, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged and new prescriptions to improve adherence.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
